events.title: Senate Acquits President Andrew Johnson
events.description: On May 26, 1868, the U.S. Senate ended its impeachment trial of President Andrew Johnson. In the final votes it fell one vote short of the two-thirds majority needed to convict him, so he stayed in office.
events.significance: The acquittal set a lasting precedent. Presidents are not removed over political disagreements with Congress, and impeachment is reserved for serious misconduct.

events.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average Debuts
events.description: Charles Dow first published the Dow Jones Industrial Average on May 26, 1896. It tracked a small group of leading American industrial companies.
events.significance: The Dow became one of the world's best-known gauges of the stock market and of the health of the U.S. economy.

events.title: Operation Dynamo Begins at Dunkirk
events.description: On May 26, 1940, Britain launched Operation Dynamo. It aimed to evacuate Allied troops trapped by advancing German forces on the northern coast of France. Over the following days, naval ships and civilian boats rescued about 338,000 soldiers.
events.significance: The evacuation saved the core of the British army. It let Britain keep fighting in World War II and became a symbol of resilience.

events.title: U.S. and Soviet Union Sign the ABM Treaty
events.description: On May 26, 1972, Richard Nixon and Leonid Brezhnev signed the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty in Moscow. It sharply limited the missile-defense systems each superpower could build.
events.significance: It was a landmark of Cold War arms control. It helped ease tensions during the era of détente.

events.title: Birth of Miles Davis
events.description: Trumpeter and bandleader Miles Davis was born on May 26, 1926. He went on to shape several eras of modern jazz.
events.significance: Albums such as Kind of Blue made Davis one of the most influential musicians of the 20th century.
